verdict.stance: Overweight / A3 Pan-African Multilateral DFI (194% LCR)
verdict.summary: AFC is a treaty-backed pan-African infrastructure DFI rated A3 (Moody's) with $14.4bn assets, 194% LCR (>34 months liquidity), and Preferred Creditor Status across 40+ African member states. Active 2025-2026 capital optimization ($500m hybrid, $700m ARISE IIP monetization, $500m Jul-31 bond) supports spread pickup over A-rated peers.

positives: Preferred Creditor Status across 44 African member states and A3 Moody's rating.
Robust liquidity (194% LCR, >34 months coverage) and consistent net profit (~$400m FY24).
Diversified funding across $5bn GMTN, $1.5bn syndicated loan, and $500m hybrid equity-credit buffer.
negatives: Concentrated sovereign/infrastructure exposure to Nigeria (~25%+) and Sub-Saharan project credits (e.g., $600m Dangote Fertiliser facility).
High single-borrower concentration relative to multilateral peers like Afreximbank.
African sovereign debt restructuring precedents test Preferred Creditor Status boundaries.

background.business_overview: Treaty-established multilateral finance institution funding African infrastructure, energy, and heavy industry.
background.asset_perimeter: $14.4bn balance sheet spanning power, transport, heavy industry, and natural resources across Africa.
background.ownership_governance: 44 African member states & institutions (Central Bank of Nigeria ~42%, African banks/DFIs).

recent_drivers: Jul-26: Issued $500m 5.375% 5-year Eurobond due Jul-2031; Apr-26 $650m notes matured & paid.
2025-26: Closed $500m perp hybrid (XS2933422888), $1.5bn syndicated loan, and $700m ARISE IIP stake monetization.

catalysts.impact: Confirms FY25-FY26 asset scale, NPLs, and Basel/prudential capital ratios.
Evaluates A3 rating headroom post-Dangote/Angola deployments.

management_guidance_tracker.variance_analysis: Hybrid bond + ARISE IIP exit strengthened equity buffer.

management_questions.question: Provide FY25/H126 exact NPL ratio, Stage 2 exposures, and sovereign exposure breakdown (Nigeria, Ghana, Zambia).
